newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's Verbund 96 pretax up, net down.
newsitem.headline: Austria's Verbund 96 pretax up, net down.

text.p: Austrian national grid company Verbund said on Tuesday 1996 group pretax profit rose to a record 1.524 billion schillings from 1.412 billion a year ago, helped by the company's cost savings programme.
Net profit inched down to 1.3 billion from 1.381 billion in 1995, while sales were up at 20.037 billion schillings from 19.635 billion, Verbund said in a statement released ahead of a news briefing.
Verbund said it had cut the number of its employees by 171 to 4,420 at year-end, bringing the total number of jobs cut over the past three years to 750.

"We will press on with our restructuring programme and continue on the path to becoming one of the European Union's most modern electricity providers," chief executive Hans Haider was quoted as saying.

Verbund, which supplies some two-thirds of Austria's electricity needs, has previously said restructuring measures should result in annual cost savings of at least one billion schillings from the year 2003.

At the start of the year, the company restructured its business into four individual operative units responsible for power generation, transmission, sales, and other activities. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 274
